claims.text: ASTM F3269-21, an active ASTM standard practice last updated on 19 November 2021, provides an architectural framework for a run-time assurance (RTA) system as an alternative to design-time assurance for meeting safety requirements of an unassured or complex function in aircraft systems; its scope includes RTA components and determining safe boundaries and RTA coverage.
claims.scope: ASTM public product page for a paywalled standard practice
claims.challenge: Do not imply regulator acceptance for a specific product, or that an RTA framework resolves a monitor that cannot observe the relevant perception failure.

claims.text: FAA AC 20-152A (October 2022) describes an acceptable, non-exclusive means of compliance for the electronic-hardware aspects of airborne systems and recognizes ED-80/DO-254.
claims.scope: FAA public advisory circular; not DO-254 text
claims.challenge: Not ML-specific; do not infer how an authority treats a GPU running a neural network.

claims.text: FAA AC 20-193 (January 2024) gives an acceptable means of compliance for multi-core processors in airborne systems, warning that interference between applications on a multi-core processor could make safety-critical software behave non-deterministically or unsafely or miss its execution time; its objectives do not apply where cores act only as co-processors or graphics processors under the control of another core and linked only by conventional avionics databuses.
claims.scope: FAA public advisory circular on multi-core processors
claims.challenge: State the exception precisely; it depends on configuration and is not a general exemption for GPUs.

claims.text: NASA-STD-7009B, approved 5 March 2024, sets requirements and recommendations for developing and using models and simulations, aiming to reduce the risks of simulation-influenced decisions through a life-cycle process with formal credibility assessments; it states what must be accomplished and communicated, not how.
claims.challenge: A NASA standard; use it as a public example of simulation-credibility practice, not as a road or aviation requirement.

claims.text: The STPA Handbook (Leveson and Thomas, 2018) describes STPA as a hazard analysis technique that, in addition to component failures, treats accidents as possibly caused by unsafe interactions among components that have not failed and may satisfy their requirements.
claims.challenge: A method description; its use in a specific regulatory regime needs separate sourcing.

claims.text: The EU Publications Office catalogs UN Regulation No 157, uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to automated lane keeping systems, as EU publication 2021/389.
claims.challenge: Title-level evidence; do not infer content, amendments or speed limits from it.
